stories.title: A Bangladesh textile factory with lawns wins the RIBA International Prize
stories.summary: The Green Field Factory of Karupannya Rangpur Limited, a seven storey rug and textile factory in Rangpur designed by Nakshabid Architects, won the RIBA International Prize on 15 October. Workers take breaks in lawns and courtyards that recall old zamindari mansions. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: A Surrey leisure centre aims for Passivhaus and 60 per cent less energy
stories.summary: Willmott Dixon has signed a pre-construction agreement with Waverley Borough Council for the new Cranleigh Leisure Centre, designed to the Passivhaus standard. It is expected to cut operational energy demand by around 60 per cent against a typical leisure centre. Work starts in early 2027, opening in autumn 2028.

stories.title: San Diego breaks ground on its first mass timber affordable housing
stories.summary: Father Joe's Villages broke ground on an eight storey, 124 apartment affordable housing block at 16th Street and Island Avenue in East Village, built in mass timber. A 2021 code update allowed mass timber up to 18 storeys. Steel and concrete, KPBS notes, need huge amounts of energy.

stories.title: Critics question the Port of Portland's mass timber tenant
stories.summary: Environmental groups have asked the Port of Portland to fully vet Zaugg Timber Solutions, the Swiss owned key tenant of its mass timber campus at the former Terminal 2, and to disclose lease details. They say the project is led by someone previously accused of mishandling a similar one.

stories.title: Two Brooklyn Passive House renovations, built by the same early adopters
stories.summary: A Passive House Accelerator piece describes two Brooklyn renovations, Carriage House and Cobble Hill, built by contractors who helped shape the designers' method. Taffera Fine Building completed the first Passive House in Manhattan, and Kleen Construction the first certified one in a landmarked district.

stories.title: A Seoul hyperscale data centre gets LEED Gold
stories.summary: IGIS Asset Management says its 80 megawatt Samsong Data Center northwest of Seoul has received LEED Gold under the Building Design and Construction system, with a design meant to cut energy consumption by 49 per cent. It is the second data centre in South Korea to reach Gold.

stories.title: THISS Studio designs buildings around whatever materials turn up
stories.summary: London practice THISS Studio, founded by Tamsin Hanke and Sash Scott, starts projects from salvaged barn beams, a pontoon boat or a dismantled exhibition, letting available materials shape the design, designboom reports. Its motto is that dismantling should be designed, not improvised. The drawing comes after the skip.

stories.title: A Lugano installation treats old cars as future building material
stories.summary: It All Remains, by Giona Bierens de Haan for the 2026 i2a Biennale del Territorio in Lugano, explores obsolete cars as building stock. Switzerland has nearly five million registered vehicles, and around 200,000 leave circulation each year, about two thirds of them exported to countries with looser rules.

stories.title: Malaysian industrial parks now compete on green credentials
stories.summary: Industrial park developers in Malaysia are competing on renewable energy access, flood mitigation, green building certification and worker housing as export manufacturers demand them, Kenanga Research says. Its report assessed five developers including Sime Darby Property and Eco World Development. Location, location, solar panels.

stories.title: Jamie Durie returns with a second season of Future House
stories.summary: Designer Jamie Durie's Future House, whose premiere led its timeslot with 570,000 viewers, is back for a second season on Australia's housing shortage. The first season showed homes could be built in weeks rather than months. Durie has called it the biggest housing crisis Australia has had.

stories.title: Bihar Museum ranks ninth among the world's 100 best museums
stories.summary: The Bihar Museum in Patna is ninth in the world and first in Asia on Worth a Journey's World's 100 Best Museums 2026 list, placing it above the Louvre and the Met, The Indian Express reports. The Louvre will be fine, probably.

stories.title: CEPT study finds the Ahmedabad bhavan where Sardar Patel served is quake resistant
stories.summary: A CEPT University student project assessed the Grade I Sardar Patel Bhavan at the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation for soil settlement and seismic compatibility. The 1885 brick masonry building has a jack arch roof and timber trusses. The researchers also suggested structural strengthening.

stories.title: Calcutta High Court calls Kolkata's oldest buildings the city's pride
stories.summary: A Calcutta High Court judge said buildings at 9, 10 and 11 Jawaharlal Nehru Road are among Kolkata's earliest and must not be damaged. The three storey building at number 9, built in 1787, is regarded as the oldest standing private building in the city.

stories.title: Coimbatore courts move out of a damaged heritage building
stories.summary: Courts in the colonial era heritage building of Coimbatore's combined court complex are to be shifted after structural damage, on directions from Madras High Court Justice P. Velmurugan. Lime plaster fell from a ground floor ceiling on 19 September, and rain worsened the building's condition.

stories.title: ArchDaily on how India builds around water, from coastal roads to data centres
stories.summary: An ArchDaily essay argues that in India, water remains a shared ecological resource while the land around it is financed and defended as an economic asset. It starts with Mumbai's Coastal Road, noting the city has historically been built by displacing water.

stories.title: Mumbai SRA change shrinks construction area for sea facing projects
stories.summary: The Slum Rehabilitation Authority has revised permissions to calculate floor space index on net instead of gross plot area, affecting over 45 redevelopment projects in areas such as Bandra and Juhu, ET Realty reports. The municipal corporation is worried about lower premium revenue.

stories.title: A house for three generations goes vertical on a tight plot
stories.summary: Space Agency's 3,500 square foot Vaastavya Residence, completed in 2024, replaces an ageing family home on a compact plot with vertical living and controlled privacy. The clients, Vageesh Hegde and Sindhu, both in software, wanted a home built around togetherness.

stories.title: Agartala slum residents get Light House Project flats after eight years
stories.summary: After eight years, 278 lower income residents of a slum along the Haora river were allotted flats in the Agartala Light House Project under Tripura's affordable housing scheme. The project is aligned with the Centre's Global Housing Technology Challenge for disaster resistant construction.

stories.title: Noida amends its master plan to find land for farmers' plots
stories.summary: The Noida Authority has amended Master Plan 2031 so pending plots promised to farmers whose land was acquired can be planned next to village settlements. Around 12,800 beneficiaries are still waiting. Most of Noida has already been developed, which made finding the land difficult.

stories.title: Bengaluru office rents rise as fast as Tokyo's
stories.summary: Bengaluru recorded an 11.5 per cent rise in prime office rents in the July to September quarter, matching Tokyo and ranking fourth of 24 Asia Pacific markets, Knight Frank says. Mumbai's year to date leasing has already passed its full total for 2025.

stories.title: Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is Architecture MasterPrize design of the year
stories.summary: The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora has been named the 2026 Architectural Design of the Year by the Architecture MasterPrize, with Snøhetta, JLG Architects and Confluence among its designers. The competition drew thousands of submissions from 95 countries.

stories.title: Australia's National Architecture Awards go to Yitpi Yartapuultiku and The Forest
stories.summary: The Australian Institute of Architects handed out 44 awards and commendations from 62 shortlisted entries. Yitpi Yartapuultiku in Port Adelaide, by Ashley Halliday Architects with an Aboriginal working group and Wax Design, won three, including public and sustainable architecture.

stories.title: Inter and Milan unveil a €1.2bn stadium to replace San Siro
stories.summary: Inter and Milan revealed the 71,500 seat Generali Stadium, which will replace San Siro from the 2031 to 32 season at a cost of €1.2bn. Some fans at the launch unfurled a banner reading 'You will never extinguish the lights at San Siro.'

stories.title: Herzog and de Meuron will turn a Birkenstock warehouse into the Eames Institute museum
stories.summary: Herzog and de Meuron is reworking the former Birkenstock campus in Novato, California, into the museum of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity, keeping its sculptural concrete roof. It will house exhibitions, workshops and public gardens, with opening targeted for 2030.

stories.title: Stefano Boeri wins the Loco Park masterplan in Tbilisi
stories.summary: Stefano Boeri Architetti will turn a former Soviet era electric locomotive plant in Tbilisi's Temka district into a residential neighbourhood around parks. The 73,600 square metre plan proposes nine buildings with about 120,000 square metres of floor area, shops on the ground and apartments above.

stories.title: Thomas Phifer's TR Warszawa theatre finally joins its museum twin
stories.summary: The dark TR Warszawa Theatre now stands beside the white Museum of Modern Art on Warsaw's Plac Defilad. Phifer won the competition for both buildings more than a decade ago. The museum opened first while the theatre stayed on the boards.

stories.title: Sunderland's National Glass Centre edges towards demolition
stories.summary: Historic England has recommended a certificate of immunity from listing for the 1998 National Glass Centre, and the culture secretary is said to be minded to grant it. The University of Sunderland plans to demolish the building, citing repair costs of up to £45 million.

stories.title: Schindler's Lovell Beach House is for sale for the first time in 100 years
stories.summary: Rudolph Schindler's 1926 Lovell Beach House in Newport Beach is on the market for $18.8 million, having stayed in the Lovell family for a century. Philip and Leah Lovell, its clients, believed in fresh air, natural light and outdoor living.

stories.title: Vinci's Warbud will build Poland's largest concert hall
stories.summary: Warbud, Vinci's Polish subsidiary, has won a €149m contract for the second phase of Sinfonia Varsovia Centrum in Warsaw, a 1,877 seat concert hall designed by Atelier Thomas Pucher. It will include a 400 seat chamber hall and a 400 metre suspended promenade.

stories.title: AIA Los Angeles names its 2026 design award winners
stories.summary: The AIA Los Angeles chapter honoured 20 projects across typology categories in its 2026 Design Awards, starting with affordable housing such as Little Berkeley in Santa Monica by Brooks Scarpa. The organisers said design excellence matters more than ever.

stories.title: Büro Ziyu Zhuang scatters a museum cluster across a meadow in Xianning
stories.summary: On the edge of Zishan Lake in Hubei, Büro Ziyu Zhuang placed four cultural buildings, a main museum, a meditation tower, a rammed earth workshop and a bookshop, across a meadow. Together they cover roughly 3,900 square metres.

stories.title: An Olympic Airways data centre becomes a medical school in Athens
stories.summary: Buerger Katsota Architects and MCA converted the former data centre and offices of Olympic Airways, next to the Ellinikon development, into UNIC Athens Medical School. The 1980s building was upgraded to current standards in less than 20 months from start to operation.

stories.title: Olaver builds a glass block garden studio in Melbourne
stories.summary: Australian practice Olaver designed Laneway Studio, a two storey garden building with a glass block facade set in recycled white brick, for a family of five. It was a practical alternative to renovating the main house, and it glows like a lantern at night.

stories.title: Al-Jawad Pike gives Aesop's Harrods counter a terracotta makeover
stories.summary: London studio Al-Jawad Pike has redone Aesop's counter in Harrods with terracotta tiles, aiming for 'the qualities of a miniature building' with apertures, openings and floor levels. Aesop has had a counter there for over a decade. Skincare now comes with floor plans.

stories.title: India's cement sector uses less energy, but worker safety is worsening
stories.summary: An iFOREST report finds India's cement industry uses about 2.54 gigajoules per tonne against a global average of 2.88, but renewables make up only 5.1 per cent of its energy mix. It also flags rising groundwater use in water stressed areas and worsening worker safety.

stories.title: JK Lakshmi Cement breaks ground on an ₹11,000 crore Assam plant
stories.summary: JK Lakshmi Cement has started work on Project Kamakshi, an integrated cement plant at Umrangso in Dima Hasao with 2.5 million tonnes a year of cement capacity. The project, the company's first in the Northeast, is targeted for completion by FY2029.

stories.title: India's copper use rises 12 per cent, with buildings among the drivers
stories.summary: India's copper consumption grew 12.1 per cent in FY26 to 2.1 million tonnes, the International Copper Association India says. Infrastructure grew fastest on solar and wind additions, while buildings, data centres, commercial space and premium homes also added demand.

stories.title: A 19th century dogtrot house plan gets a prefab Passive House cottage
stories.summary: Toronto studio Williamson Williamson reworked the open air dogtrot layout, designed for the heat of the American South, into a 1,500 square foot prefab cottage in Magnetawan, Ontario. It has a highly insulated envelope and a layout that can shrink in colder months.

stories.title: Soundproofing and acoustic treatment are different jobs
stories.summary: Architecture Lab explains that soundproofing stops sound passing between rooms through mass and airtight layers, rated by STC, while treatment controls echo inside a room, rated by NRC. Foam panels count as treatment. They will not stop the neighbour's television.

stories.title: A webinar series tackles mass timber engineering in Canada
stories.summary: Canadian Consulting Engineer will run Mass-Timber Engineering Challenges on 17 November, 24 November and 1 December for licensed engineers. Four speakers will cover design coordination, timber procurement, scheduling, building envelope optimisation and fenestration integration.

stories.title: AUDA plans a ₹175 crore green headquarters aiming for IGBC Platinum
stories.summary: The Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority plans an 11 floor, 45 metre headquarters at Bhat on the Sardar Patel Ring Road, on an 11,760 square metre plot. Officials target an IGBC Platinum rating with about 88 points, using orientation based facades and other passive features.

stories.title: Ahmedabad's pols show how shared walls and courtyards handle heat and community
stories.summary: Outlook Traveller looks at Ahmedabad's pols, residential clusters entered through a gate called a khadki, with closely packed houses sharing walls along narrow streets. Shaded courtyards and shared spaces show what it calls climatic ingenuity, along with doorsteps where neighbours stop to talk.

stories.title: A 1961 Kochi home keeps laterite walls and red oxide floors
stories.summary: Designer Sreejith Jeevan's two storey home near Fort Kochi, built by his grandfather in 1961, keeps the Kerala vocabulary of laterite walls, red oxide floors and wooden doors and windows, Architectural Digest India reports. He calls it his version of Kerala Modern.

stories.title: Bhubaneswar launches a digital twin that maps heat stress street by street
stories.summary: The Bhubaneswar Climate Digital Twin lets residents check heat stress, waterlogging and air pollution for neighbourhoods, streets and buildings. Built by the municipal corporation with technical support from GIZ India, it is described as India's first platform of its kind.

stories.title: BRICS cities report asks Mumbai to treat cooling as a productivity issue
stories.summary: The summary report of the BRICS Friendship Cities Conclave 2026, led by Mumbai First and presented to the Maharashtra Governor, recommends treating heat as a cost to productivity and energy use. It urges climate responsive buildings, green infrastructure and early warning systems.

stories.title: IGBC asks Hyderabad's water board to revive blocked rainwater pits
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council has asked HMWSSB to restore defunct rainwater harvesting pits across the old GHMC area to arrest a falling groundwater table. IGBC chairman C. Shekhar Reddy said poor maintenance had left most pits blocked, and offered help to secure a silver rating.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir's unified building byelaws need GIS rules, an op-ed argues
stories.summary: A Brighter Kashmir op-ed says the Unified Building Byelaws enacted in 2021 are being undermined by amendments and questions whether one code suits J&K's diverse landscape. It proposes a rule based GIS system for building permissions with automatic compliance checks.

stories.title: Architects explain why the same material behaves differently across India's climates
stories.summary: Construction World asks how materials affect energy efficiency. Architect Dikshu Kukreja says that in India's varied climates the same material behaves differently depending on thickness, orientation and exposure. Tejbeer Singh says material choice is one of the earliest chances to shape performance.

stories.title: World Energy Savings Day piece makes the case for cooler buildings
stories.summary: An Energetica India commentary for World Energy Savings Day on 21 October argues energy efficiency is a climate and economic matter and an investment in a heat resilient future. Its central line is that the cleanest unit of energy is often the one not consumed.

stories.title: Larger blocks of similar buildings make cities cooler, a 101 city study finds
stories.summary: A study of 101 cities published in PNAS on 19 October finds that grouping buildings with the same function into larger continuous blocks weakens daytime surface heat islands. The authors, from Ghent, Cambridge, Imperial and others, call this dimension invisible to conventional analysis.

stories.title: Delhi renovates 1,200 rainwater harvesting systems
stories.summary: The Delhi Jal Board has renovated nearly 1,200 rainwater harvesting systems and plans regular inspections to keep them working, officials told PTI. A proposed Rainwater Harvesting Policy 2026 will align with Master Plan Delhi 2047 to tackle waterlogging and recharge groundwater.

stories.title: World Cities Day 2026 focuses on housing
stories.summary: World Cities Day on 31 October, hosted in Fuzhou, China, takes the theme Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All. According to the United Nations, up to 3.4 billion people lack access to adequate housing, secure tenure, basic services or affordable living conditions.

stories.title: Business Standard argues India's cities cannot be run from state capitals
stories.summary: A Business Standard editorial backs NITI Aayog member Rajiv Gauba's view that cities need more autonomy for urban local bodies. India's urban population is projected to rise from about 500 million to 850 million by 2050, adding pressure on housing and transport.

stories.title: India Foundation paper says city systems are the missing link in growth plans
stories.summary: An India Foundation paper notes cities generate nearly 60 per cent of India's GDP and an estimated 70 per cent of new jobs by 2030 will be urban. Allocations for cities have totalled over ₹8 lakh crore, and it argues city systems need reform.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh's draft housing policy ties subsidies to income
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh's draft Urban Affordable Housing and Habitat Policy 2026 sets separate support for EWS, LIG and MIG households, Urban Acres reports. EWS households earning up to ₹3 lakh a year would get ₹2.5 lakh per unit. Income decides the land model too.

stories.title: How Smart City and AMRUT projects are reshaping urban Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: A Times of India report says Uttar Pradesh's urban push over nine years has used the Smart Cities Mission for technology, mobility and public spaces, and AMRUT 2.0 for drinking water, sewerage and water conservation, extending beyond the big metros.

stories.title: Nagpur may waive ₹40,000 a day penalties on delayed Smart City works
stories.summary: A review committee of Nagpur's Smart City corporation is inclined to waive delay penalties of ₹40,000 a day. Contractors say tender terms cap penalties at ₹20,000 and blame land handover delays, utility shifting and the monsoon. The deadline, meanwhile, has been very understanding.

stories.title: Ho Chi Minh City picks a twisting tower for a port interchange
stories.summary: Ho Chi Minh City has approved a design with a twisting tower among elevated roads, ponds and green spaces for an interchange on the nearly 6 km Cat Lai to Phu Huu port access road. It links Vietnam's busiest container port to Ring Road No 3.

stories.title: World Bank warns Africa's cities need jobs and infrastructure to match growth
stories.summary: A World Bank Group report, Sub-Saharan Africa's Urban Awakening, says the region's urban population could reach about 1.7 billion by 2050. Weak planning, limited industry and thin public finance risk trapping millions in informal work, it warns.

stories.title: Former Palantir executives launch Dream, an AI building design startup, with $17M
stories.summary: Dream Technologies, founded by former Palantir executives Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur, launched with a $17 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz. The company says its models can generate hundreds of design variations in a few minutes. Architects used to call that a charrette.

stories.title: Origin raises $20M for robots that finish interiors
stories.summary: San Francisco startup Origin has emerged from stealth with $20 million, co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures, to deploy its OG-1 robot for interior construction. Pilots include two of the largest drywall finishing contractors in the US and Europe. Drywall finishing has found its disruptor.

stories.title: Maximo's construction robots pass 300,000 solar installation tasks
stories.summary: Maximo Robotics says its robots have completed more than 300,000 tasks on US utility scale solar projects, with crews installing 2.5 times faster per person per shift hour than by hand. Contractors pay per task completed instead of buying the machines.

stories.title: Nemetschek bundles AI into Archicad, Allplan and Bluebeam
stories.summary: Nemetschek Group has launched premium AI versions, Archicad Max, Allplan Max and Bluebeam Max, all on its Nemetschek Intelligence Platform. The company says the AI takes on repetitive work while keeping professionals in control of every decision.

stories.title: Noida signage firm Kreative Brain passes 1,000 projects
stories.summary: Kreative Brain, a Noida signage design and fabrication company, says it has delivered more than 1,000 projects for over 274 clients, from illuminated hotel facades in the Himalayas to hospital wayfinding in the NCR. It says developers now treat signage as part of the architecture.

stories.title: Why AI designed buildings all start to look the same
stories.summary: A Parametric Architecture essay notes that AI generated buildings increasingly share one visual language of sculptural curves, dramatic cantilevers, seamless glass and carefully controlled light. The results can be beautiful, it says, which makes the sameness harder to notice.

stories.title: designboom podcast gathers Indian architects on architecture that listens
stories.summary: Room for Utopias, a designboom podcast made with INDX Global during designboom paris, gathers Indian architects and designers across eleven conversations filmed in Paris. It skips grand urban visions for grounded propositions already in practice.

stories.title: Pratt faculty present books on clay, 3D printing and AI at ACADIA
stories.summary: Pratt's Jonathan A. Scelsa presented Claying Architecture, on clay as a meeting point of 3D printing and traditional practice, at the ACADIA 2026 Book Forum in Detroit. Jonas Coersmeier presented Material and Artificial Intelligence in Architecture, focused on AI ethics.

stories.title: Architecture MasterPrize names the best architectural photography of 2026
stories.summary: Derry Ainsworth won top honours for Hong Kong Modern Mosaics, a series of tightly framed facades, in the 2026 Architecture Photography MasterPrize. Tzu Chin Yu of TCY Studio won interior photography for a study of the Kanazawa Umimirai Library.

stories.title: A London architect is fined £2,500 over inadequate drawings
stories.summary: The Architects Registration Board fined Melanie Schubert of SAM Architects £2,500 for unacceptable professional conduct, finding she gave inadequate design information and did not properly inspect works before certifying completion on a Victorian house renovation finished in 2021.

stories.title: Can design respond to superstitious thinking?
stories.summary: The Spaces looks at how superstition shapes design, starting with the quiet omission of the 13th floor. Interiors photographer Mark C O'Flaherty says we all take spiritual, superstitious design on board subliminally. The lift buttons agree.

stories.title: Dezeen opinion calls Trafalgar Square's Lady in Blue a monument to our era
stories.summary: Priya Khanchandani writes that Tschabalala Self's Fourth Plinth sculpture, Lady in Blue, unveiled in September, belongs in Trafalgar Square. The commission has raised questions about who belongs in public space and who gets cast in bronze.

stories.title: A Nebraska student 3D prints a model of a proposed middle school
stories.summary: Hayden Hauser 3D printed a model of the proposed Gering Middle School with a removable roof to show its layout, presenting it at the Gering Public Schools district office, the Star-Herald reports. Most school projects get a poster.

research.title: A Reproducible Inertia Dynamometer for Vocational Schools: Design, Fabrication, and Pedagogy
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the design, construction, and classroom use of an inertia dynamometer, built as a year-long project-based learning (PBL) activity with adult students at a Greek Evening Vocational High School (EPAL). The apparatus consists of a. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Counterfactual assessment of social media interventions by separating exposure from engagement
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Social media interventions are usually evaluated in individual-level experiments, which are costly to scale and often miss collective effects. We propose the Exposure--Engagement model, whose parameters separately control what social media users are exposed to (recommendation). Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CrowdEgress: A Multi-Agent Simulation Platform for Pedestrian Crowd
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article introduces a simulation platform to study complex crowd behavior in social context. The agent-based model is extended based on the social force model, and it mainly describes how agents interact with each other, and. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Early-Buyer Groups and Fast-Wallet Teams on a Bonding-Curve Launchpad: A Prospective Measurement Study of pump.fun on Solana
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We study coordinated groups of wallets on a bonding-curve launchpad (pump.fun on Solana), using a complete record of 200\,443 token launches, 15\,854\,121 curve trades and 51\,025\,958 SOL transfers over 88.3 hours. A prospective, multi-channel discovery procedure. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Emergence, Asymmetry, and Value in AI Networks: An Anoptical Perspective
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This chapter presents exploratory experiments suggesting that asymmetry and functional value hierarchy emerge among LLM-based agents sharing the same context, although they are equivalent and interact within a symmetric network. We use the Poietic Generator, a. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From Airspace Degradation to Deconfliction: Predicting Safety-Critical Traffic States through the Evolution of Multiscale Complexity Metrics
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Growing air traffic demand is pushing airspace management towards the limits of its operational capacity, with steadily increasing workload for air traffic control officers, with direct consequences for safety. Understanding which traffic conditions give rise to. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and R\'enyi entropy. We. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Large scientific teams are more, not less, disruptive
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern science has moved decisively toward larger and more collaborative research teams. Yet an influential 2019 study reported that small teams are more disruptive than large teams, a conclusion difficult to reconcile with both the well-known. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
